listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Sunday, November 15. Here is what is worth your time today. Our lead story is about public health. The United States has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated. That is according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization. Global health authorities are said to have reached this view. Official details are still to come. Now the front page. In the UFC, Kayla Harrison submitted Amanda Nunes with a rear-naked choke in Round 4 at UFC 334. It was enough to keep her title. From Anthropic, the company announced an expanded partnership with the General Services Administration to bring Claude to all levels of government. And for the 49ers, tackle Trent Williams and linebacker Dre Greenlaw are listed as questionable for today's game against the Cowboys. Receiver Mike Evans has been ruled out. In tech and AI, Anthropic says its AI for Science program is expanding to foundations and research institutions. Two trending repos are worth a look. One lets coding agents control a live Chrome browser. The other is a workspace for reviewing and sending feedback to agents. In politics, Drop Site's daily reports an Iranian strike on a U.S. radar in Bahrain, a challenge by Senator Chris Van Hollen to Chuck Schumer, and talk of a possible Cuba operation. The Lever covers a report alleging corruption behind a New Mexico data center project. And the Trump administration's plan to sell some public lands is drawing bipartisan opposition. In world news, Pope Leo spoke of community suffering during a visit to a remote Andes town. In the United States, the transport secretary says a copper wire upgrade was behind the flight suspension. In sports, Ciryl Gane edged Josh Hokit in a five-round fight to keep his heavyweight title. Stephen Thompson ended his career with a spinning kick knockout. And the NBA suspended Rockets guard Marcus Smart for three games over a punch. In Atlanta, a street overhaul is set to begin in Little Five Points. A condo tower of up to 225 feet is proposed in Old Fourth Ward. And a 21-acre park is about to open in an underserved area. In architecture, McNeel is bringing AI into Rhino 9. Archiboost raised six point two million dollars for its AI platform. And a tool called qentin makes scanned buildings searchable in plain language. In science and nature, a new documentary follows scientists exploring the Southern Ocean. Chandra data explain outbursts from a giant unstable star. And Honduras declared an environmental emergency in its largest protected area. That is the brief. Have a good day. This is the Sunday edition. Here is the week in review. Anthropic files for IPO as Ukraine talks resume. Anthropic made the biggest news in your core topics. It filed an S-1 with the SEC for a proposed initial public offering, launched its roadshow and committed a portion of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund (w76, w56, w57). It also released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, with a faster, higher-priced mode for Fable 5.2 (w27, w31). The Claude Platform now offers self-hosted Managed Agents (w102). In design software, Chaos, Trimble, McNeel and SketchUp all added AI or BIM features (w20, w45, w95, w70). In world news, U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi ended with an agreement on a prisoner exchange. U.S. envoys then met Putin (w79, w109). The White House says Trump, Putin and Xi plan a joint meeting in China next week (w123). After the midterms, House Republicans chose Jim Jordan as their leader. Democrats won the Mississippi Senate race and the Alaska governor's race (w61, w78, w125). A building collapse in Brooklyn killed at least two people (w89), and a nationwide ground stop disrupted U.S. air travel (w122). In sports, Alperen Sengun scored 43 points in a Rockets win (w124), and the 49ers acquired receiver Keenan Allen (w80). The Braves agreed to a three-year, $35 million deal with Evan Phillips (w103), and Kayla Harrison submitted Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 (w146). In Atlanta, Beltline housing projects kept moving (w42, w94), and the Chattahoochee RiverLands project secured 327 more acres (w93).

lead.title: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
lead.note: The United States has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated. That is according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization, as reported by NPR. The summary does not give further detail, such as dates or case counts, so those remain to be confirmed. In plain terms, elimination status is a formal designation that health authorities grant to a country, and losing it means that designation no longer applies. The report relies on sources with knowledge of the deliberations, and the headline attributes the finding to global health authorities. For readers, the practical point is that this is a notable change in the country's public health standing, and further official statements will show how the decision is made public and what follows from it.
